newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Three Bangladeshis die of AIDS - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Three Bangladeshis die of AIDS - newspaper.

text.p: Three Bangladeshis have died of AIDS and 65 others have been found to be HIV-positive, the Financial Express newspaper said on Monday.

Sixty-eight out of 40,000 people tested over the last three years had been found carrying the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which causes the Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), the newspaper said, quoting experts at a health seminar in Chittagong on Saturday.
Of the 68, 10 people had developed AIDS. Three of the AIDS patients had died and seven were seriously ill, the paper said.
It quoting unidentified physicians as saying Bangladesh, an overwhelmingly Moslem country, might have four million AIDS patients by the end of the century. It did not give any details.

With AIDS spreading alarmingly in neighbouring India and Burma, Bangladesh could face great danger from the killer disease unless vigorous precautions and an awareness drive were put in place immediately, the newspaper added.
It said some 9.5 million people, including 1.5 million children, were suffering from AIDS in Asia alone.

The term AIDS applies to the most advanced stages of HIV infection. By killing or impairing cells of the immune system, HIV progressively destroys the body's ability to fight infections and certain cancers.
HIV is spread by sexual contact with an infected partner or through contact with infected blood.
